analysis:
Examined both test-document excerpts, model-revision file metadata and its complete supplied patch. The test excerpts (docs/developer/test.md:2731–3434) are unchanged according to the complete range map; they describe tenant partitioning, media admission, memory accounting, cancellation, pairing and qualification limits, not new serving controls. The changed test documentation at 2115–2131 describes credential-free workflow fixtures and explicitly does not establish model quality or capacity.
The added publication runbook (docs/operations/model-revisions.md:171–296) introduces CI reconstruction and public object upload, with manifest equality to locally qualified bytes, immutable reservation, manifest-last publication and separate registration/promotion. These contracts relate to A-004, T-012/T-027 and T-007; revision-bound cache identity also matters to T-041. Documentation alone establishes no concrete bypass or security regression. It expressly distinguishes repository legacy secrets from environment-gated secrets; their historical availability is not evidence of a newly introduced leak.
Integration must verify .github/workflows/model-requant-upload.yml, scripts/models/requant.py, its input/manifest validators and publish-model-revision.py: ref and approval gates, actual secret scope, hostile input handling, pinned-source/download behavior, complete artifact equality and immutable upload semantics. Environment reviewer/branch settings asserted in the runbook are not independently verified here. Determine whether the new CI publication authority requires an explicit threat-model boundary; it must not be conflated with signed-build qualification or serving authorization. Missing implementation is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety or a finding.
